concepts.name: Arranging distinct objects
concepts.description: Ordering n objects, or r of them chosen from n.

concepts.name: Repeated objects
concepts.description: Dividing out the arrangements that identical items duplicate.

concepts.name: Arrangements with conditions
concepts.description: Items that must stay together, or must not.

formulas.title: Fundamental principle of counting
formulas.prompt: A task has m ways for the first step and n for the second. How many ways in total?
formulas.explanation: Independent choices multiply. Choices that are alternatives to each other add instead.
formulas.commonMistake: Adding when the steps happen together rather than as alternatives.
formulas.applicationPrompt: You pick one of 3 shirts and one of 4 trousers. How many outfits?

formulas.title: Arranging n distinct objects
formulas.prompt: In how many ways can n distinct objects be arranged in a row?
formulas.explanation: The first position has n choices, the next n − 1, and so on down to 1.
formulas.commonMistake: Using 4 × 4 × 4 × 4, which allows repetition that a row of distinct books does not have.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many ways can 4 distinct books be arranged on a shelf?

formulas.title: Permutations of r from n
formulas.prompt: How many ways can r objects be chosen AND arranged from n distinct objects?
formulas.explanation: Fill the r positions in turn: n choices, then n − 1, and so on for r factors.
formulas.commonMistake: Using it when order does not matter — that is a combination.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many ways can 2 prizes be given to 5 different people, one each?

formulas.title: Arrangements with repeated items
formulas.prompt: How many distinct arrangements are there when some objects are identical?
formulas.explanation: Swapping two identical letters produces the same word, so divide by the arrangements of each repeated group.
formulas.example:
LEVEL: 5 letters with L twice and E twice
= 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 30
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to divide, which counts each distinct word several times.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many distinct arrangements does the word LEVEL have?

formulas.title: Items that must stay together
formulas.prompt: Two people must sit next to each other. How do you count the arrangements?
formulas.formula: Treat the pair as one block: (n − 1)! × 2!
formulas.explanation: Glue the pair into a single unit, arrange the units, then arrange the pair internally.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting the internal 2! for the pair's own order.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 5 people sit in a row and two of them must be adjacent. How many arrangements?

formulas.title: Never together = all − together
formulas.prompt: How many arrangements keep two particular people apart?
formulas.explanation: Counting the arrangements where they are together is easy (treat them as one block); subtract from the total.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting that the pair can stand in 2 orders inside the block.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In how many ways can 6 books be shelved so that two given books are not side by side?

formulas.title: Letters with a block of vowels
formulas.prompt: How do you count arrangements of a word with all the vowels together?
formulas.formula:
Treat the vowels as one letter: (consonants + 1)! × (vowels)!
Divide by k! for each letter repeated k times
formulas.explanation: The block moves as one unit; inside it the vowels can still be arranged.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to divide for the repeated E.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In how many ways can the letters of TRIANGLE be arranged with the vowels together?

levels.title: Counting Without Listing
levels.description: Multiply choices, and decide whether order matters before touching a formula.

blocks.title: Choices multiply
blocks.body:
If you pick a shirt in 3 ways and trousers in 4, there are 3 × 4 = 12 outfits. Every shirt pairs with every trouser.

That is the fundamental principle of counting, and almost everything else in this topic follows from it.
'And' usually means multiply; 'or' usually means add. Shirt AND trousers → 3 × 4. Bus OR train → 3 + 4.

blocks.title: Arranging is repeated choosing
blocks.body:
Four books on a shelf:
first slot 4 ways, then 3, then 2, then 1
= 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 4! = 24

blocks.title: The question to ask first
blocks.body:
Does order matter? Prize-giving, seating and forming numbers care about order — those are permutations. Selecting a team or a committee does not — those are combinations.

Classify first, calculate second. Most errors here are classification errors.

questions.question: In how many ways can 4 different books be arranged on a shelf?
solutionSteps: First position: 4 choices.
Then 3, then 2, then 1.
questions.method: n! for arranging n distinct objects.

hints.text: Once a book is placed, it cannot be used again.
Multiply 4 × 3 × 2 × 1.

questions.question: What is the value of ⁵P₂?
questions.method: Multiply r descending factors starting at n.

hints.text: Two positions to fill: 5 choices then 4.
Multiply those two counts together: 5 × 4.

questions.question: How many 3-digit codes can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if no digit may repeat?
solutionSteps: First digit: 5 choices.
Second: 4 remaining. Third: 3 remaining.
questions.method: Fill positions one at a time, reducing the pool.

hints.text: Each digit used removes an option for the next position.

questions.question: How many 3-digit codes can be formed from the digits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if a digit may be repeated?
questions.explanation: Each of the 3 places can be filled by any of the 5 digits, because digits may repeat. Ways = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125.
solutionSteps: Hundreds place: 5 choices.
Tens place: still 5 choices, since repetition is allowed.
Units place: 5 choices.
questions.method: Repetition allowed: the pool does not shrink, so multiply 5 three times.

hints.text: Repetition is allowed, so how many choices does each place have?
Multiply the choices for the three places.

commonMistakes: Reducing the pool each time (5 × 4 × 3 = 60), which is the no-repetition answer.

questions.question: Which of these situations requires a PERMUTATION rather than a combination?

options.text: Awarding gold, silver and bronze medals to 3 of 8 runners
Choosing 3 students from 8 to form a committee
Selecting 3 books from 8 to take on holiday
Picking 3 toppings from 8 for a pizza

questions.explanation: Medals are distinguishable, so the order of selection changes the outcome. Committees, book selections and toppings are unordered.
solutionSteps: Ask whether swapping two chosen items changes the outcome.
Gold and silver swapped is a different result — order matters.
So it is a permutation.
questions.method: Classify by whether order changes the outcome.

hints.text: Would the people involved care which of them got which position?

commonMistakes: Treating any 'choose r from n' wording as a combination.

questions.question: For the same n and r (with r ≥ 2), ⁿPᵣ is always greater than ⁿCᵣ.
questions.explanation: ⁿPᵣ = ⁿCᵣ × r!, and r! > 1 when r ≥ 2, so the permutation count is always larger.
solutionSteps: Every selection of r items can be arranged in r! orders.
ⁿPᵣ = ⁿCᵣ × r!.
For r ≥ 2, r! ≥ 2, so ⁿPᵣ > ⁿCᵣ.
questions.method: Relate the two counts through r!.

hints.text: Each unordered selection corresponds to how many ordered ones?

commonMistakes: Assuming the two are equal when r = n.

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements can be made of the letters of the word LEVEL?
questions.explanation: 5 letters with L twice and E twice: 5! ÷ (2! × 2!) = 120 ÷ 4 = 30.
solutionSteps: Total letters = 5, so 5! = 120 if all were distinct.
L repeats twice and E repeats twice.
questions.method: Divide by the factorial of each repeated group.

hints.text: Which letters appear more than once?
Swapping the two Ls gives the same word, so those arrangements are double-counted.

questions.question: In how many ways can 5 people be seated in a row if two particular people must sit next to each other?
questions.explanation: Treat the pair as one block: 4 units arrange in 4! = 24 ways, and the pair can swap internally in 2! ways, giving 48.
solutionSteps: Glue the two people together: now there are 4 units.
Arrange the units: 4! = 24.
The pair can sit in 2 orders internally: 24 × 2 = 48.
questions.method: Block method, then multiply by the internal arrangements.

hints.text: Think of the pair as a single person for a moment.
That gives 4 units to arrange.
Do not forget the pair can swap places.

questions.question: In how many ways can the letters of the word GARDEN be arranged so that the two vowels are always together?
questions.explanation: GARDEN has 6 different letters, with vowels A and E. Tie the vowels into one block: the block and G, R, D, N make 5 units, arranged in 5! = 120 ways. Inside the block A and E can swap in 2! = 2 ways. Total = 120 × 2 = 240.
solutionSteps: Vowels: A, E. Consonants: G, R, D, N.
Treat AE as one block: 5 units in all.
Arrange the 5 units: 5! = 120.
Arrange the vowels inside the block: 2! = 2.

hints.text: Glue the two vowels together and count the block as one letter.
How many units are there to arrange now?
Do not forget that A and E can swap places inside the block.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the 2! for the order inside the block (120).

questions.question: How many 4-letter arrangements (words, meaningful or not) can be formed from the letters of MONDAY, with no letter repeated?
questions.explanation: MONDAY has 6 distinct letters, so ⁶P₄ = 6 × 5 × 4 × 3 = 360.
solutionSteps: MONDAY has 6 distinct letters.
Four positions to fill in order: 6 × 5 × 4 × 3.
questions.method: ⁶P₄ — order matters because these are words.

hints.text: Are all six letters different?
Four positions, filled from a shrinking pool.

commonMistakes: Using ⁶C₄ = 15, which ignores the ordering of letters in a word.

questions.question: How many distinct arrangements can be made of the letters of the word BANANA?
questions.explanation: 6 letters with A three times and N twice: 6! ÷ (3! × 2!) = 720 ÷ 12 = 60.
solutionSteps: BANANA has 6 letters: B, A×3, N×2.
Divide by 3! for the As and 2! for the Ns: 720 ÷ 12 = 60.
questions.method: Divide by the factorial of each repeated group.

hints.text: Count how many times each letter appears.
A appears 3 times and N appears twice.

commonMistakes: Dividing by only one of the repeated groups.

questions.question: How many 4-digit even numbers can be formed from the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 if no digit may be repeated?
questions.explanation: Split by the units digit. If it is 0, the other three places take any 3 of the remaining 5 digits in order: ⁵P₃ = 60. If it is 2 or 4, the thousands digit cannot be 0 or the units digit, leaving 4 choices, and the middle two places take 4 × 3 = 12 ways: 2 × 4 × 12 = 96. Total = 60 + 96 = 156.
solutionSteps: An even number ends in 0, 2 or 4.
Units digit 0: the rest is ⁵P₃ = 60.
Units digit 2 or 4: thousands digit has 4 choices (not 0, not the units digit).
Middle two digits: 4 × 3 = 12, so 2 × 4 × 12 = 96.
questions.method: Fill the restricted places first, and split into cases when 0 is involved.

hints.text: Fill the units place first, since it must be even.
Zero is special: it cannot go in the thousands place.
Count "ends in 0" and "ends in 2 or 4" separately, then add.

commonMistakes: Treating all three even endings alike (3 × 4 × 4 × 3 = 144).
Forgetting that 0 cannot be the first digit.

questions.question: In how many distinct ways can the letters of the word BALLOON be arranged so that the two Ls are next to each other?
questions.explanation: BALLOON has 7 letters: B, A, L, L, O, O, N. Treat LL as one block. That leaves 6 units — LL, B, A, O, O, N — with O repeated twice: 6! ÷ 2! = 360. The two Ls are identical, so swapping them inside the block gives nothing new.
solutionSteps: Letters: B, A, L, L, O, O, N (L twice, O twice).
Glue LL into one block: 6 units.
Only O is still repeated among the units.
Arrangements = 6! ÷ 2! = 720 ÷ 2 = 360.
questions.method: Block the identical pair, then divide by the factorials of what is still repeated.

hints.text: Treat the two Ls as a single block.
After blocking, which letter is still repeated?
Identical letters inside a block cannot be swapped.

commonMistakes: Not dividing by 2! for the two Os (720).
Still dividing by 2! for the Ls after they are blocked (180).
